list.title: Open for Tourism:
list.snippet: Turkey is generally open to tourists, including U.S. citizens, and you can obtain an e-Visa for tourism or commerce purposes online.

list.title: Visa Requirements:
list.snippet: U.S. citizens can stay for up to 90 days without a visa for tourism or commerce.

list.title: Passport Validity:
list.snippet: Ensure your passport is valid for at least six months beyond your intended stay.

list.title: Increased Caution:
list.snippet: The U.S. Department of State (.gov) advises increased caution due to terrorism, armed conflict, and potential for arbitrary detentions.

list.title: Specific Areas:
list.snippet: Do not travel to Sirnak province, Hakkari province, or any area within 10 kilometers of the Syrian border due to ongoing risks.

list.title: Monitor Alerts:
list.snippet: Stay informed about current events and potential risks by checking travel advisories from the U.S. Department of State (.gov) and Turkish authorities.

list.title: Register with STEP:
list.snippet: Enroll in the Smart Traveler Enrollment Program (STEP) to receive security updates and allow the embassy to locate you in an emergency.

list.title: Be Aware of Your Surroundings:
list.snippet: Pay attention to your surroundings, especially in crowded tourist areas, and avoid drawing attention to yourself.

list.title: Trust Your Gut:
list.snippet: If a situation feels unsafe, remove yourself from it.
Demonstrations: Be aware of the potential for demonstrations and protests and avoid areas where they are taking place.
Enhanced Security: Expect increased security measures and police presence.
Follow Local Advice: Adhere to instructions from local authorities.
Pack Appropriately: Dress conservatively, especially when visiting mosques or conservative areas.
Share Your Plans: Let someone know your itinerary and check in regularly.
